title: Pin warnings (example)
summary:
An example page for the help-me-spec-interactive skill, with every question and visual type it supports: a pair of boards, a board per option, a line to step through, a Mermaid flow, a multi-choice question and a defaults section.

The feature is made up to show the format. Its questions and recommendations are illustrations, not decisions for any project.

questions.question: Which of these knights is pinned?
questions.context: In both positions the bishop on b5 attacks the knight on c6, with d7 empty behind it. In A the king stands on e8, so the knight has no legal move. In B Black has castled and a rook stands on e8: the knight can move, and `Bxe8 Qxe8` then wins the exchange.

options.label: A only
options.description: Absolute pins: only the king behind. The knight has no legal move, so the warning is never wrong.

options.label: A and B
options.description: Absolute and relative pins: any more valuable piece behind. Players call both pins.

questions.question: How should the board mark a pin?

options.label: The whole line
options.description: Pinning piece, pinned piece and the squares to the king.

options.label: The pinned piece
options.description: Only c6; the text names the pinning bishop.

questions.question: Should a pin that one move can break still be reported?
questions.context: Focus the board, then step with the arrow keys: `5.d4` attacks e5, which the pinned knight cannot defend, and `5...Bd7` breaks the pin.

options.label: Yes, every pin
options.description: The position is what it is; breaking the pin is the answer the player should find.

options.label: Only lasting pins
options.description: Skip pins a block or a king move ends at once. Needs a one-move search.

options.label: A derived detector
options.description: Reads an attack map that other detectors can share.

options.label: A board detector
options.description: Walks the lines itself: no dependency, repeated work.

questions.question: Which pinning pieces should be reported?

sections.title: Defaults I'll use unless you object
sections.intro: Small decisions I would otherwise make without asking. Choose No where you disagree.
